I really like the story interludes, they make the game events so much more personal. Like when one of my bases was attacked by a Gaian mindworm swarm and obliterated. You get a really sad sob story about how your favorite subordinate was killed horribly and you dedicate a memorial to the base. The terraforming is really fun too, watching the entire planet transform from human activities gives a really interesting perspective and it makes me think about how we've changed our planet so much. The unit designer is real cool too, gives you so much more strategic/tactical flexibility and it lets you choose how much you want to spend on your soldiers. Instead of just equipping the most expensive and new technology, you can go cheap. It appeals to my inner-cheapskate.

AC is one of my favorite Civ games, and it's one of the only games I've bought twice: on CD when it came out, then on GOG a couple of years ago. (I loved the story so much I even bought the tie-in novels. They were...not good.)

And now I want to play it again. So long, free time.

I still play it occasionally. I really like how the factions and their leaders felt detailed and unique, each with their own personalities. I loved reading the quotes from each of them.

I also liked how the factions didn't represent nationalities like in other Civ games, but were instead based on ideologies. It kind of took all these competing political theories, threw them onto a hostile alien planet, and said "may the most practical ideas win." That sort of intellectual Darwinism makes for a very interesting and appealing game.
You hit the nail on the head! I loved the idea of playing based on anything other than nationalities.
